source.title: Investigating Sensitive Directions in GPT-2: An Improved Baseline and Comparative Analysis of SAEs

record.tranche_reason: The study revisits the claim that SAE reconstruction errors are pathologically harmful, comparing them with improved random-direction baselines and across SAE types.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports results for SAE feature directions, but those do not measure SAE reconstruction errors and are not rows here.
record.test_reason: The study reruns Gurnee's substitution test of SAE reconstruction errors on GPT2-small. It finds the errors exceed isotropic random perturbations but roughly match covariance-matched and real-activation mixture baselines. This is a direct argument that V3's 'pathological' claim depends on the baseline chosen.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that SAE errors are no longer pathologically large against realistic (mixture) baselines, though this varies across layers. They also find GPT2-small is more sensitive to lower-L0 SAE feature directions, and that e2e SAE features are not more influential than traditional SAE features. The record omits the L0 finding.
record.recipe_differences: The study revisits SAE reconstruction-error KL comparisons using the established substitution-style sensitive-direction measurement, and adds cov-random mixture and real mixture baselines plus comparisons across L0 and SAE types.
record.method_sensitivity: The reconstruction-error comparison varies by layer, SAE type, L0, and perturbation length.

fits_no_version.finding: The previously reported pathological excess of SAE errors is largely explained by the anisotropy of real activations, which an isotropic random baseline ignores.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The apparent pathology of SAE errors is an artifact of an isotropic random baseline. It is not a property of the SAE's training or of the model's structure.

fits_no_version.finding: Perturbing along SAE feature directions shifts outputs more than isotropic random directions. Lower-L0 features shift them more, and e2e SAE features are not more influential than local SAE features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How much SAE feature directions influence outputs depends on L0 and on the SAE training type.

record.peer_reviewed: Workshop on Attributing Model Behavior at Scale at NeurIPS 2024
record.problems: The main summary uses mean KL, which the authors say may oversimplify the curves. Many comparisons are described qualitatively without numerical values in the text, and the improved-baseline comparison varies across layers.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reconstruction-error results were left out. SAE feature-direction findings were omitted because they measure feature directions rather than reconstruction errors.

untested.parts: Not tested: no linear prediction of the error from the input activation.
Not tested: no per-token error-norm prediction across SAE sizes, and no scaling analysis.
Not tested: no split of the error into linear and nonlinear parts.
Not tested: no circuit or steering analysis with or without the error term.
Not tested: the size of the error is not measured across training choices. The study only compares how sensitive the model is along error directions for local, e2e and e2e+ds SAEs.
Effect on cross-entropy loss is not measured; only next-token KL is used. The model is GPT2-small only.

missing.what: Which layers still show an SAE(x) KL excess over the mixture baselines, and the size of that excess per layer
Numeric KL values for SAE(x) and each baseline; only qualitative descriptions are in the text

record.verdict_notes: The study is a NeurIPS 2024 workshop paper. All comparisons are qualitative, with no numbers in the text. The isotropic-baseline result confirms Gurnee's original observation; the main contribution is the mixture baseline that removes the excess. The V6 links were removed because error size is never compared across architectures here.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of the error vector is a linear function of the input activation.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, whether larger and smaller SAEs fail on the same contexts, and whether error persists with scale.
The comparison concerns next-token KL under activation substitution, not a direct test of the error's effect on all model computations.
Whether the linear component reflects unlearned features and whether the nonlinear component resists further dictionary learning.
Whether circuits, steering, or other feature-based analyses lose behavior when the error term is omitted.

The study compares reconstruction-error effects across SAE types and L0 settings, but does not isolate sparsity penalties, shrinkage, dead latents, or objective choice as causes, nor establish that better architectures or end-to-end training generally shrink the error.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: Substituted SAE reconstruction activations and compared next-token KL with isotropic random substitutions at the same distance.
rows.measure: Mean KL divergence of next-token predictions
rows.baseline: Isotropic random point at the same distance
rows.value: SAE reconstruction substitution changes next-token probabilities significantly more than isotropically random substitution.
rows.note: The text describes the comparison but gives no numeric KL values.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE reconstruction substitutions with cov-random mixture and real mixture perturbations.
rows.measure: Mean KL divergence of next-token predictions
rows.baseline: Cov-random mixture and real mixture directions
rows.value: SAE reconstruction KL is generally closer to the mixture baselines, with considerable variation by layer.
rows.note: The text says the improved baselines mitigate the previously observed high-KL behavior, but reports layer-dependent variation.
rows.check: The state is fine: SAE(x) KL is 'generally closer' to the mixture baselines but varies considerably by layer. The text does not say which layers keep an excess.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: Compared Layer 6 SAE reconstruction-error perturbations with cov-random mixture perturbations across SAE L0 settings.
rows.measure: Mean KL divergence of next-token predictions
rows.value: The SAE models across L0 generally have nearly the same KL as cov-random mixture.
rows.note: The paper presents this as evidence that the previously reported pathologically high KL is mitigated by addressing isotropy.
rows.check: Remove the V6 link. The row compares KL across L0 against the cov-random mixture and says nothing about training choices making the error smaller. Also, the paper cites Figure 5 for this claim, but Figure 5's caption describes feature directions, so the locator may be mislabelled.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.2, final paragraph; Section 2 for the default activation site.
source_check.problem: The paragraph supports the result, but its Figure 5 reference is inconsistent: Figure 5 concerns feature directions rather than reconstruction substitutions.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE reconstruction substitutions, mixture perturbations, and isotropic random substitutions across SAE models.
rows.baseline: Isotropic random substitutions; cov-random mixture and real mixture also compared
rows.value: Isotropic random substitutions have much smaller average KL; SAE(x), cov-random mixture, and real mixture generally have similar average KL.
rows.note: The appendix describes qualitative comparisons across SAE models without giving numeric values.
rows.check: The row mixes two baselines and should be split. Against isotropic random the excess is observed (isotropic KL is 'much smaller'). Against cov-random and real mixture it is absent (they are 'generally similar' to SAE(x)) across several SAE models, including Bloom's and Braun's local SAEs.

source_check.correct: Split by comparator: observed against isotropic random substitution; absent against cov-random mixture and real mixture, whose average KL is generally similar to SAE(x). Section 2 specifies approximately 2 million Openwebtext tokens for these experiments.
source_check.locator_found: Appendix A, Figure 6 caption; Section 2, Data.
source_check.problem: A single partial state conflates observed and absent excesses against different baselines; the token count is stated globally.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: Extrapolated local SAE reconstruction-error directions over perturbation lengths and compared their KL curves with mixture baselines.
rows.baseline: Cov-random mixture and isotropic random directions
rows.value: Local SAE curves are close to the cov-random mixture curves; lower L0 corresponds to a stronger perturbation effect.
rows.note: The text describes the curves qualitatively and does not give numerical values.
rows.check: Remove the V6 link. Local SAE error-direction curves are close to the cov-random mixture, so there is no excess sensitivity beyond the realistic baseline. The L0 dependence (lower L0 gives a stronger effect) is a side result.

source_check.problem: The absent state applies to excess over the cov-random mixture comparator; it should not be read as absence of an effect relative to isotropic noise.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: Extrapolated e2e SAE reconstruction-error directions over perturbation lengths.
rows.baseline: Cov-random mixture and isotropic random directions
rows.value: The curves remain low and then rise sharply from around perturbation length 50; at lengths below 50, lower L0 generally gives greater KL, except for e2e L0 = 21.0 or 27.5.
rows.note: The authors state that e2e SAEs generally have high L2 reconstruction error while having low KL divergence.
rows.check: Remove the V6 link. The e2e error-direction curves stay low and then spike near length 50. Whether they fall below or above the baseline depends on perturbation length, and the actual error length is not given, so the version's effect cannot be read. The note 'e2e SAEs have high L2 error, low KL' is the authors' expectation drawing on Braun et al. (ref [10]), not a result measured here.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: Extrapolated e2e+ds SAE reconstruction-error directions over perturbation lengths.
rows.baseline: Cov-random mixture and isotropic random directions
rows.value: The curves remain low and then rise sharply from around perturbation length 50; at lengths below 50, lower L0 generally gives greater KL, except for e2e L0 = 21.0 or 27.5.
rows.note: The text groups e2e and e2e+ds results for this description.
rows.check: Remove the V6 link. The text groups e2e+ds with e2e, and the exception for L0 = 21.0/27.5 applies to e2e only, not e2e+ds. The row's value copies that exception wrongly.

source_check.correct: For e2e+ds, curves remain low before rising sharply around perturbation length 50. Below 50, the text states that lower L0 produces greater KL; above 70, it states that lower L0 produces a stronger effect. The L0 = 21.0 or 27.5 exceptions apply only to e2e SAEs.
source_check.problem: The copied L0 exceptions identified in the pack belong to e2e, not e2e+ds.

relation.reason: Its own GPT2-small reconstruction-substitution and error-direction experiments directly compare SAE errors with random perturbation baselines.

tranche.reason: The study reproduces the isotropic comparison while arguing that structured baselines remove or reduce the apparent pathological excess, qualifying V3.

source_check.notes: The authors-conclusion paraphrase is supported. Verdicts concern prediction KL, not demonstrated cross-entropy harm; the paper also cautions that mean KL can obscure variation among individual perturbation curves.

statements.correction: Reported output measure: mean next-token KL divergence. Cross-entropy comparison against structured mixture baselines: not reported. Explicit declaration that cross-entropy is untested: absent.
statements.problem: The paper does not explicitly list cross-entropy as untested; that is an inference from its reported methods and results.

statements.correction: Feature-direction outcome: next-token KL under perturbations along alive, context-inactive SAE features. Sensitivity depends on L0 and SAE training method. Task-directed steering efficacy: not measured.
statements.problem: The reconstruction-error summary is supported, but steering efficacy exceeds the feature-direction experiment's measured outcome.
